We are looking to add top talent to our Baptist Hospitals of Southeast Texas team. 

Join us in performing Sacred Work!

Competitive benefits are offered including:

Matched Retirement Plan

Paid Time Off

Comprehensive Benefit Plan – Medical, Dental, Vision and Much More!

Bonus Potential

 

Summary/Objective 

The Clinical Dietitian provides assessment, diagnosis, intervention, monitoring and evaluation of patients identified as potential nutritional risk and coordination of MNT, as well as assists in the administrative and technical management of the Food and Nutrition Department

Essential Job Duties 

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  1. Maintain Daily Censes Sheets for assigned units; to screen for and track nutrition assessments, follow-ups and all other nutrition intervention.
  2. Provides MNT to all patients requiring nutrition intervention; perform nutrition assessment of patients identified at nutrition risk, Develops, implements and, per policy, documents an individualized plan of care for each patient in the EMR ; monitors patient response to planned intervention through reassessment, addressing previously identified nutrition related problems; provides nutrition counseling and educations to patient/caregivers.
  3. Monitors enteral and parenteral nutrition support, diets and menus for adherence to therapeutic modifications and diet consistency and communicates with staff as needed to maximize patient care.
  4. Educates and serves as expert reference point to patients, families, and staff on home alternative nutrition and hydration services. Works with DME and insurance companies to help coordinate care for patients as needed. 
  5. In collaboration with CNM, the RD acts as a preceptor for the Dietetic Internship program
  6. Completes audit logs relating to patient care and food preparation as well as productivity logs, supplement logs and other Clinical Nutrition logs as assigned.

Required Education and Experience

Bachelor of Science in Nutrition and Dietetics, completion of a Dietetic Internship program.

Required License/Certifications

Current CDR for Registered Dietitians and Licensure Designation

item.title: Registered Nurse - Trauma Program Registrar - Per Diem / Flex - Days
item.description: We are looking to add top talent to our Baptist Hospitals of Southeast Texas team. Join us in performing Sacred Work! Competitive benefits are offered including: Matched Retirement Plan Paid Time Off Comprehensive Benefit Plan – Medical, Dental, Vision and Much More! Bonus Potential Summary/Objective The Trauma Registrar is responsible for the management of the Trauma Registry, data collection, data entry, data quality and integrity which is vital in supporting the Trauma Performance Improvement and Patient Safety program. Provides advanced critical thinking skills utilizing nursing judgement to extrapolate all pertinent trauma diagnoses, procedures and complications after thorough review of the medical record. Performs Utilization Review on trauma and trauma surgery admissions. Is an active participant in quality meetings conducted by Trauma Services. A. Assessment: the registered nurse collects comprehensive data pertinent to the patient’s health or the situation and enters this data into the Trauma Registry. B. Diagnosis: the registered nurse analyzes the assessment data to determine the diagnoses or issues. C. Outcomes Identification: the registered nurse identifies expected outcomes for a plan individualized to the patient or the situation. D. Planning: the registered nurse develops a plan that prescribes strategies and alternatives to attain expected outcomes. E. Implementation: the registered nurse implements the identified plan, coordinates care delivery, employs strategies to promote health and a safe environment. F. Evaluation: the registered nurse evaluates progress toward attainment of outcomes. G. Quality of Practice: the registered nurse systematically enhances the quality and effectiveness of nursing practice. Essential Job Duties Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Utilizes a systematic approach to provide individualized, goal-directed, nursing care by performing comprehensive nursing assessments regarding the health status of the patient, making nursing diagnoses that serve as the basis for the strategy of care, developing a plan of care based on the assessment and nursing diagnosis, implementing nursing care, and evaluating the patient's responses to nursing interventions. Make assignments others that take into consideration patient safety and that are commensurate with the educational preparation, experience, knowledge, and physical and emotional ability of the person to whom the assignments are made (in compliance with the Texas Nurse Practice Act). Maintains required documentation of patient care and unit activities in accordance with standards. Clarify any order or treatment regimen that the nurse has reason to believe is inaccurate, non-efficacious or contraindicated by consulting with the appropriate licensed practitioner and notifying the ordering practitioner when the nurse makes the decision not to administer the medication or treatment. Know the rationale for and the effects of medications and treatments and shall correctly administer the same to promote a safe environment for patients and others. Ensures compliance with DSHS standards as a Level III Trauma Center. Performs concurrent and/or retro chart audits on patients admitted in the ED with traumatic diagnosis. Enters or supervises entry of necessary data into the Trauma Registry and reviews statistics. Responsible for review of all necessary information and required forms on all trauma diagnosis and transfers. Promotes the benefits of an organized trauma service system to professional and community groups. Participates in community educational programs, interacts with local EMS community Required Education and Experience Graduate of an accredited nursing program 2-3 years related experience in surgical, critical care or emergency nursing. Required License/Certifications Current RN License in the state of Texas BLS certification ACLS certification PALS or ENPC certification TNCC certification Preferred or within 60 days of hire: Association for the Advancement of Automotive Medicine (AAAM) course, American Trauma Society (ATS) Trauma Registrar Course. Obtain the American Trauma Society Certified Specialist Trauma Registry (CSTR) within 18 months of hire
item.taleo:html-description:
We are looking to add top talent to our Baptist Hospitals of Southeast Texas team. 

Join us in performing Sacred Work!

Competitive benefits are offered including:

Matched Retirement Plan

Paid Time Off

Comprehensive Benefit Plan – Medical, Dental, Vision and Much More!

Bonus Potential

Summary/Objective 

The Trauma Registrar is responsible for the management of the Trauma Registry, data collection, data entry, data quality and integrity which is vital in supporting the Trauma Performance Improvement and Patient Safety program. Provides advanced critical thinking skills utilizing nursing judgement to extrapolate all pertinent trauma diagnoses, procedures and complications after thorough review of the medical record. Performs Utilization Review on trauma and trauma surgery admissions. Is an active participant in quality meetings conducted by Trauma Services.

A. Assessment: the registered nurse collects comprehensive data pertinent to the patient’s health or the situation and enters this data into the Trauma Registry.

B. Diagnosis: the registered nurse analyzes the assessment data to determine the diagnoses or issues.

C. Outcomes Identification: the registered nurse identifies expected outcomes for a plan individualized to the patient or the situation.

D. Planning: the registered nurse develops a plan that prescribes strategies and alternatives to attain expected outcomes.

E. Implementation: the registered nurse implements the identified plan, coordinates care delivery, employs strategies to promote health and a safe environment.

F. Evaluation: the registered nurse evaluates progress toward attainment of outcomes.

G. Quality of Practice: the registered nurse systematically enhances the quality and effectiveness of nursing practice.

Essential Job Duties 

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  1. Utilizes a systematic approach to provide individualized, goal-directed, nursing care by performing comprehensive nursing assessments regarding the health status of the patient, making nursing diagnoses that serve as the basis for the strategy of care, developing a plan of care based on the assessment and nursing diagnosis, implementing nursing care, and evaluating the patient's responses to nursing interventions.
  2. Make assignments others that take into consideration patient safety and that are commensurate with the educational preparation, experience, knowledge, and physical and emotional ability of the person to whom the assignments are made (in compliance with the Texas Nurse Practice Act).  Maintains required documentation of patient care and unit activities in accordance with standards.    
  3. Clarify any order or treatment regimen that the nurse has reason to believe is inaccurate, non-efficacious or contraindicated by consulting with the appropriate licensed practitioner and notifying the ordering practitioner when the nurse makes the decision not to administer the medication or treatment.  Know the rationale for and the effects of medications and treatments and shall correctly administer the same to promote a safe environment for patients and others.
  4. Ensures compliance with DSHS standards as a Level III Trauma Center. Performs concurrent and/or retro chart audits on patients admitted in the ED with traumatic diagnosis. 
  5.  Enters or supervises entry of necessary data into the Trauma Registry and reviews statistics.  Responsible for review of all necessary information and required forms on all trauma diagnosis and transfers.  
  6. Promotes the benefits of an organized trauma service system to professional and community groups.  Participates in community educational programs, interacts with local EMS community

Required Education and Experience

Graduate of an accredited nursing program

2-3 years related experience in surgical, critical care or emergency nursing. 

Required License/Certifications

Current RN License in the state of Texas

BLS certification

ACLS certification

PALS or ENPC certification

TNCC certification  

Preferred or within 60 days of hire: Association for the Advancement of Automotive Medicine (AAAM) course, American Trauma Society (ATS) Trauma Registrar Course.

Obtain the American Trauma Society Certified Specialist Trauma Registry (CSTR) within 18 months of hire
